newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah firmer on liquidity fears.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah firmer on liquidity fears.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah was firmer against the dollar in slow late trading on Monday on fears of a liquidity squeeze this week, dealers said.
They said trading was slow, with fears of possible tightening on Tuesday causing operators to unload dollars.
One foreign bank dealer said players seemed to revert to liquidity issues in the afternoon, shrugging off initial worries over the heated campaign for the May 29 general elections
Spot rupiah was at 2,426.5/27.0 at 0915 GMT after easing to a low of 2,428.0. It opened at 2,426.5/27.5. Tomorrow and today rupiah closed at 2,426.5/27.0 and 2,426.5/27.25, respectively.
Dealers said the market fluctuated within a narrow range between 2,426.5 and 2,427.5 during the day.
They said the rupiah strengthened at the opening in line with the weakening dollar against major currencies, but was later overwhelmed by fears over the election campaign.
However, liquidity became the focus later.
Dealers said anticipation of higher weekly tax payments due on Tuesday came to the fore, driving short-dated swaps up.
Tom/next swaps were at 0.55/0.60. Overnight swap closed at 0.6/0.7 points and overnight money was last at 10.0 percent.
One U.S. bank dealer said moves to increase dollar holdings to factor in campaign worries were limited by expensive short-dated swaps which increased the price of going long.
"People seem to hold on to small long dollar positions only. Others are seen cashing out at cost," she said.
Dealers said longer-term swaps edged up slightly on the back of the tighter liquidity outlook and uncertainty over the on-going election campaign.
One-month swaps edged up to 14.10/14.75 from 12.50/13.25, two to 26.5/27.0 from 25.0/26.0, three to 39.00/39.25 from 37.5/38.0 and six to 77.0/77.5 from 75.25/75.75 points.

Dealers said there was no immediate response in the market to central bank governor Sudradjad Djiwandono's comments that he was worried about the recent rise of the yen against the dollar, as much of the country's external debt is denominated in yen.
He also said the rupiah had depreciated three to five percent annually since the early 1980s, and said he had been "comfortable" with the depreciation.
"When we talk about the depreciation of the rupiah, it's part of our efforts to support the export drive to help our competitiveness in exports," he said.
Djiwandono said there was room for lower interest rates in Indonesia when inflation was under control.
However, interest-rate trends in major nations such as the United States were complicating Indonesia's moves on interest rates, he added.
The central bank lowered its intervention band by one point to 2,406/2,598 and the conversion band also by one point to 2,406/2,454 on Monday, following a similar one-point appreciation on Friday.
